title: The maths behind machine learning
promise: Learn it alone, then explain it to someone else.

modules.title: Foundations
modules.summary: The high-school maths everything else rests on, taught from pictures first.
outcomes: Read and rearrange simple equations, and explain why one equation with two unknowns has many solutions
Explain what a logarithm counts and why it squeezes huge ranges
Read Σ notation and the common symbols used in machine-learning papers

concepts.title: Variables and expressions
objectives: Explain a variable as a labelled box that holds a number
Evaluate a simple expression for a given value
takeaways: A letter stands for a number that can change or is not yet known.
An expression is a recipe that turns the numbers in the boxes into a new number.
Naming things lets us state a rule once and use it for every value.

concepts.title: Equations
objectives: Explain an equation as a rule linking quantities, not an instruction
Describe why one equation with two unknowns gives a line of solutions
Solve two equations for two unknowns
takeaways: An equation states that two things are equal; it is a rule, not a command.
One equation with two unknowns leaves a whole line of answers.
A second independent equation usually pins the answer down to one point.

concepts.title: Functions and graphs
objectives: Describe a function as a machine with one output per input
Read a value from a graph
takeaways: A function turns each input into exactly one output.
A graph draws every input-output pair at once.
Reading a graph is how you see what a function does.

concepts.title: Slope and linear functions
objectives: Compute the slope between two points
Explain what m and b mean in y = mx + b
takeaways: Slope is how much the output changes for one step in the input.
In y = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the starting value.
A neuron's weighted sum plus a bias has this same shape.

concepts.title: Exponents, growth and decay
objectives: Explain an exponent as repeated multiplication
Tell growth from decay by the size of the base
takeaways: An exponent counts how many times to multiply by the base.
A base above one grows; a base between zero and one decays.
Repeated multiplication gets large or small much faster than repeated addition.

concepts.title: Logarithms
objectives: Explain a logarithm as a count of multiplication steps
Use log(ab) = log a + log b
Name two everyday scales that are logarithmic
takeaways: A logarithm counts how many times you multiply by the base to reach a number.
It turns multiplication into addition.
It squeezes huge ranges into manageable ones.

concepts.title: Σ notation
objectives: Expand a Σ sum into its terms
Write a short sum using Σ
takeaways: Σ means add up a list of terms.
The small marks below and above say where the list starts and stops.
Dot products and loss totals are sums written this way.

concepts.title: Ratios, percentages and averages
objectives: Convert between a ratio, a fraction and a percentage
Compute a mean
takeaways: A ratio compares two amounts by division.
A percentage is a ratio out of one hundred.
A mean is the total shared out equally.

concepts.title: Sine and cosine
objectives: Describe sine and cosine as the two coordinates of a point on a circle
Say which one is the horizontal part
takeaways: Cosine and sine are the horizontal and vertical positions of a point going round a circle.
They repeat as the angle keeps turning.
Cosine of the angle between two arrows will reappear in the dot product.

concepts.title: Reading mathematical notation
objectives: Read subscripts, hats and the symbols ∈ and ∀
Recognise a bold letter as a vector
takeaways: Notation is shorthand; each mark has a plain-language reading.
Subscripts pick one item from a list.
Bold letters usually mean a vector.

modules.title: Linear algebra
modules.summary: Vectors, matrices and what they do to space. Part 1 is built; part 2 is on its way.
outcomes: Multiply a matrix by a vector and explain what it does to space
Describe a vector both as an arrow and as a list of numbers
Build new vectors from linear combinations of old ones

concepts.title: Vectors: arrows and lists
objectives: Describe a vector as an arrow and as a list

concepts.title: Adding, scaling and combining vectors
objectives: Add and scale vectors

concepts.title: Matrices: tables and machines
objectives: Read a matrix as a table and as a machine

concepts.title: Matrix-vector and matrix-matrix multiplication
objectives: Multiply a matrix by a vector

concepts.title: Linear transformations: rotate, scale, shear, project

modules.title: Analytic geometry
modules.summary: Norms, distance, the dot product, angles and projections.

modules.title: Matrix decompositions
modules.summary: Determinants, eigenvectors, SVD and low-rank approximation.

modules.title: Vector calculus
modules.summary: Derivatives, gradients, the chain rule and backpropagation.

modules.title: Probability and distributions
modules.summary: Probability rules, Bayes' theorem, random variables and common distributions.

modules.title: Continuous optimisation
modules.summary: Gradient descent, learning rate, momentum and Adam.

modules.title: Information theory
modules.summary: Surprise, entropy, cross-entropy and KL divergence.

modules.title: When models meet data
modules.summary: Loss, maximum likelihood, overfitting and validation.

modules.title: Models
modules.summary: Linear regression, PCA, mixtures and classifiers.

modules.title: Capstone: a tiny language model
modules.summary: Neurons, backpropagation, attention and a tiny next-token predictor.
